faq.q: Why do I see lightning before thunder?
faq.a: Both start together, but light travels about 300 thousand kilometres a second while sound travels only about 343 metres a second. The flash reaches you almost at once, and the sound trails behind.
asks: Why does thunder come after lightning?
Do lightning and thunder happen at the same time?

faq.q: How can I tell how far away a storm is?
faq.a: Count the seconds between the flash and the thunder. Divide by 3 for kilometres or by 5 for miles. Ten seconds means the lightning was about 3 kilometres away.
asks: What is the flash to bang rule?
How do I count how far lightning is?

faq.q: How fast is sound compared to light?
faq.a: Light is nearly a million times faster than sound in air. Light could go round the Earth seven times in a second, while sound would cover only about a third of a kilometre.
asks: How much faster is light than sound?

faq.q: When should I go inside during a storm?
faq.a: If you can hear thunder at all, you are close enough to be struck. Go into a building or a car with a metal roof straight away and wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.
asks: Is it safe outside if the storm is far?

faq.q: Does a shorter gap mean the storm is coming closer?
faq.a: Yes. If the time between flash and bang keeps shrinking, the storm is moving towards you. If it grows, the storm is moving away.
asks: How do I know if a storm is getting closer?

facts: Sound travels about 1 kilometre in 3 seconds in air, or about 1 mile in 5 seconds.
Light travels at about 300,000 kilometres per second, nearly a million times faster than sound in air.

quiz.say: You see a lightning flash and count 9 seconds before the thunder. About how far away was the lightning?
quiz.show: 9 seconds from flash to bang means about…
quiz.why: Sound takes about 3 seconds per kilometre, so 9 seconds divided by 3 is about 3 kilometres.

wrong.0: Sound travels more than one kilometre in 9 seconds; you must divide by 3.
wrong.2: Sound covers about 343 metres in just one second.
